# Machine Learning Basics
This chapter provides a comprehensive introduction to fundamental machine learning concepts.
## Key Topics
- **Supervised Learning**: Uses labeled data to learn input-output mappings. Algorithms include linear regression, logistic regression, decision trees, and random forests [source](hypatia://cite?file=ml-basics.pdf&page=1). - **Neural Networks**: Layered architectures with neurons, activation functions, and backpropagation for training [source](hypatia://cite?file=ml-basics.pdf&page=2). - **Overfitting & Regularization**: Techniques to prevent memorization including L1/L2 penalties, dropout, and early stopping [source](hypatia://cite?file=ml-basics.pdf&page=3). - **Evaluation Metrics**: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and AUC-ROC for measuring model performance [source](hypatia://cite?file=ml-basics.pdf&page=3).
## Connections
See also: [[supervised-learning]], [[neural-networks]], [[overfitting]]

# Supervised Learning
Supervised learning is a machine learning paradigm that uses labeled training data to learn a mapping from inputs to outputs [source](hypatia://cite?file=ml-basics.pdf&page=1).
## Algorithms
- **Linear Regression**: Fits a linear model for continuous prediction - **Logistic Regression**: Uses sigmoid function for classification - **Decision Trees**: Splits feature space using information gain - **Random Forests**: Ensemble of decision trees reducing overfitting
## Objective
The goal is to minimize a loss function measuring the difference between predictions and true labels.
See also: [[neural-networks]], [[overfitting]]

# Neural Networks
Neural networks are composed of layers of interconnected neurons that transform input features through learned weights [source](hypatia://cite?file=ml-basics.pdf&page=2).
## Architecture
- **Input layer**: Receives raw features - **Hidden layers**: Transform features through learned weights - **Output layer**: Produces final predictions - **Activation functions**: ReLU, sigmoid, tanh for non-linearity
## Training
Training uses backpropagation to compute gradients of the loss with respect to each weight, then gradient descent to update weights.
See also: [[supervised-learning]], [[overfitting]]

# Overfitting and Regularization
Overfitting occurs when a model memorizes training data rather than learning general patterns [source](hypatia://cite?file=ml-basics.pdf&page=3).
## Signs
High training accuracy but low test accuracy.
## Regularization Techniques
- **L1 (Lasso)**: Absolute weight penalty, encourages sparsity - **L2 (Ridge)**: Squared weight penalty, prevents large weights - **Dropout**: Randomly disables neurons during training - **Early stopping**: Halts when validation loss plateaus
See also: [[neural-networks]], [[supervised-learning]]
